per_view.notes: Slender white fuselage with tapering nose and upswept tail cone. Front-third upper-deck hump present but reads as a blocky raised box. Tall dark-blue swept fin plus horizontal stabilizers. Window line and cockpit windows visible. Engines cluster as boxy shapes near the belly/wing root, not clearly four pylon-mounted nacelles under the wings. Nose and main gear present.

Slender light fuselage with blue stripe, tapering nose, tall swept blue fin and horizontal stabilizer read well. Upper-deck hump present but sits mid-forward, a bit blocky. Engines are a jumbled dark cluster under the mid-belly, not four clearly-spaced underwing nacelles. Nose and main gear wheels visible; dashed window line and cockpit windows present.

Four dark nacelles hung under wings with plausible inboard/outboard spacing. Light fuselage, grey wings, thin blue vertical fin plus faint horizontal stabilizer line. Rounded upper crown hints at hump. Nose gear plus clustered main-gear wheels visible below body. Cockpit windows barely readable; no clear window band from head-on. Fuselage appears slightly bulbous/short-nosed.

Rear head-on: four dark nacelles hung under swept wings with visible dihedral; central rounded fuselage with a top-crown hump bulge; tall blue vertical fin. Horizontal stabilizers are thin flat slabs, low sweep. Nose plus main-gear wheel clusters visible below. Grey body/wings, blue tail — coherent. Window lines not assessable from this angle.

Top-down: slender white fuselage, tapering nose/tail cone. Four grey nacelles roughly paired, sitting near/forward of wing leading edge. Swept tapered wings, modest ~30deg sweep. Small swept tailplane and thin fin with blue centerline stripe. Elongated oval upper-deck plus dashed window line near nose reads as hump/windows. Clean assembly.

Four underwing nacelles on pylons, slender tapering fuselage, swept dihedral wings, tall dark-blue swept fin with horizontal stabs. Nose/main gear and a passenger window line with blue cheatline visible. Upper-deck hump is very subtle and short, weakening the 747-specific read; silhouette is only moderately distinctive.

Slender white fuselage with tapered nose/tail, blue cheatline and passenger window band. Small forward crown hump. Tall swept blue fin plus grey horizontal stabilizers. Wings swept but thin, slab-like. Engines read as small dark shapes clustered near wing roots/belly rather than four distinct underslung nacelles; they intermix with the central wheel cluster, muddying craftsmanship and 747 identity

Slender grey fuselage with small front hump and blue window/belt stripe. Four nacelle-like cylinders but clustered oddly and not cleanly under-slung on pylons; one looks attached low mid-body. Swept tail with dark blue fin and horizontal stabs. Landing gear present with wheel bogies. Parts intersect/float around the wing-root and engine cluster; visible seams.

Four underwing nacelles on pylons, swept tapering wings with dihedral, tall dark-blue fin plus horizontal stabilizers. Slender white fuselage with grey wings, dark window/door dashes and cockpit windows. Nose and main gear extended. Upper-deck hump is a small subtle forward blister rather than the iconic faired 747 hump, weakening the silhouette.

critic.fix_suggestion: Improve 'Partial-length upper-deck hump' (mean 5.78/10). Target the 8 anchor: distinct partial-length upper deck starting at the nose and blending down within roughly the front third of the fuselage; then the 10 anchor: iconic 747 hump: starts at the cockpit, smoothly faired into the crown, ends around one-third of the length, with a visible cockpit region on the upper lobe.
